Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 16, verses 1–9:

Makkan, up to His statement, the Exalted: "wa-in 'aqabtum" to its end. It has 7,700 letters (ahruf), 2,840 words (kalimat), and 128 verses.

Abu Umama al-Bahili, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Nahl, Allah will not hold him to account for the blessings He bestowed upon him in the abode of this world, and he will be given a reward like that of one who dies after making a good bequest." [1] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 6/135.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"Atā amr Allāh" (The command of Allah has come): meaning it came and drew near. They differed concerning what this command is.

Some said: it is the Hour (the Final Hour).

Ibn 'Abbas said: When Allah revealed "iqtarabat al-sa'ah wa-inshaqqa al-qamar" (The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split), the disbelievers said to one another: "This man claims that the Day of Resurrection has drawn near. So refrain from some of what you were doing until we see what will happen." When they saw that nothing descended, they said: "We see nothing." Then Allah revealed: "iqtaraba li-l-nasi hisabuhum" (Their reckoning has drawn near for people) [[Surah al-Anbiya': 1.]], and so on.

They became apprehensive and awaited the nearness of the Hour. When the days stretched on, they said: "O Muhammad, we see nothing of what you frighten us with." Then Allah revealed: "Atā amr Allāh" [[Surah al-Nahl: 1.]]. The Prophet (ﷺ) leapt up, and the people raised their heads. Then it was revealed: "fa-la tasta'jilūhu" (so do not seek to hasten it), and they were reassured. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his two fingers, "except that it may outrun me." [2] [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 187.]]

Ibn 'Abbas also said: The sending of the Prophet (ﷺ) was among the signs of the Hour. When Jibril passed by the people of the heavens, sent to Muhammad (ﷺ), they said: "Allahu akbar, the Hour has come."

Others said: the "amr" here is the punishment by the sword, and this is a reply to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith when he said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You..." [[Surah al-Anfal: 32.]] (to the end of the verse), seeking to hasten the punishment; so Allah revealed this verse. This is an answer in brief: al-Nadr was killed at Badr by being executed in cold blood.

Al-Dahhak said: "Amr Allah" means the rulings, the limits (hudud), and the obligations (fara'id).

The first view is more correct, because it has not reached us that any of the Companions were hasty for an obligation of Allah before it was imposed upon them, whereas those who hastened the punishment among the polytheists were many.

"Subhanahu wa-ta'ala 'amma yushrikun" (Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him).

"Yunazzilu al-mala'ikata" (He sends down the angels).

The majority of readers read it with a damma on the yaa' and a kasra on the zay with a shadda, and "al-mala'ika" in the accusative. Most people of Makka and Basra lightened it, meaning "yunzilu Allah" (Allah sends down).

Al-Mufaddal, Rawh, Suhayl and Zayd read "yanzalu" with a fatha on the yaa' and the zay, and "al-mala'ikatu" in the nominative.

Al-A'mash read "yanzilu" with a fatha on the yaa', a jazm on the nun, and a kasra on the zay, from "nuzul" (descending), and "al-mala'ikatu" in the nominative. On both of these readings the verb belongs to the angels.

"bi-l-rūh" (with the Spirit): with the revelation (wahy); he named it a spirit because hearts live by it and truth lives by it, and disbelief and falsehood die by it.

'Ata' said: with prophethood, "fitrah" (natural disposition); the Spirit meets from His command.

Qatada: with mercy.

Abu 'Ubayda: "bi-l-rūh" means "with the Spirit," that is, with Jibril.

"min amrihi 'alā man yashā'u min 'ibādihi an" (from His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, that): its position is accusative by removal of the preposition, and its sense is "bi-anna" (that), "andhirū" meaning "a'lamū" (make known), from their saying "andhir bihi" (warn him/inform him of it). It is in the accusative position by the falling of the warning upon it.

"lā ilāha illā anā fa-ttaqūni" (There is no god but I, so fear Me). "Khalaqa al-samawāti wa-al-arda bi-l-haqq, ta'ala 'amma yushrikun." "Khalaqa al-insāna min nutfatin fa-idhā huwa khasīmun mubīn" (He created man from a drop, and behold he becomes an open adversary who disputes with falsehood). Its parallel is His saying: "wa-la takun li-l-khā'inīna khasīman" (and do not be an advocate for the treacherous) [[Surah al-Nisa': 105.]]. This verse was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi when he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone and said: "O Muhammad, do you think Allah will revive this after it has decayed?" Its parallel is His saying: "awa lam yara al-insānu annā khalaqnāhu min nutfatin" (Does not man see that We created him from a drop) [[Surah Ya-Sin: 77.]] to the end of the surah, also revealed about this incident.

"wa-al-an'āma khalaqahā" (And the cattle, He created them): meaning camels, cows and sheep. "Lakum fīhā difʼun" (For you in them is warmth): meaning from their wool, fleece and hair are garments, coverings and cotton, by which they keep warm. "Wa-manāfiʻu" (and benefits): in offspring, milk, riding, carrying and other things. "Wa-minhā ta'kulūn" (and from them you eat): meaning their flesh. "Wa-lakum fīhā jamālun ḥīna turīḥūn" (And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home): meaning when they are brought back in the evening from their pastures to their resting places where they take shelter. It is said: "arāḥa fulān māshiyatahu yurīḥuhā īrāḥatan," and the place to which they are brought back is "mirāḥ."

"Wa-ḥīna tasrahūn" (and when you send them out to pasture): meaning they are driven out in the morning from their pastures to their grazing grounds. It is said: "sarraḥa māshiyatahu yusarriḥuhā sarḥan wa-surūḥan" when he sent it out to graze, and "sarahat al-māshiyatu surūḥan" when it grazed.

Qatada said: That is most wondrous when they return with their udders full and their humps tall.

"Wa-tahmilu athqālakum ilā baladin ākhara lam takūnū bāligīhi illā bi-shiqqi al-anfus" (And they carry your loads to a land you would not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves).

Ikrima: "al-balad" means Makka.

The majority read "bi-shiqq" with a kasra on the shin, which has two meanings: first, hardship and difficulty; second, half, meaning you would not have reached it except with half the strength of your selves and with the other half of your strength gone.

Abu Ja'far read "bi-shaqqi" with a fatha on the shin. Both are dialect forms, like "baraqa" and "bariqa," "Ḥaṣun" and "Ḥaṣin," "raṭl" and "riṭl."

And the verse of al-Namir ibn Taulab is recited with a kasra on the shin:
"Wa-dhī ibilin yas'ā wa-yaḥsibuhā lahu... akhī naṣabin min shiqqihā wa-du'ūb"
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/184.]]

It may also be a verbal noun from "shaqaqtu 'alayhi yashuqqu shaqqan" (I burdened him).

"Inna rabbakum la-ra'ūfun raḥīm" (Indeed your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful) to His creation, in that He created these things for them and prepared for them these benefits and conveniences.

"Wa-al-khayla wa-al-bighāla wa-al-ḥamīra li-tarkabūhā wa-zīnatan" (And horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment): meaning He created them and made them an adornment along with the benefits in them.

Some jurists used this verse as evidence for the prohibition of eating horse meat. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about eating horse meat, and he disliked it, and recited this verse: "wa-al-khayla wa-al-bighāla wa-al-ḥamīra li-tarkabūhā wa-zīnatan."

He said: "It is for riding." He recited the preceding verse, "wa-al-an'āma khalaqahā" etc., and said: "That is for eating."

He said: "The ruling on eating horse meat is prohibited in the Book of Allah," then he recited these verses and said: "He made these for eating and those for riding."

To this view went Abu Hanifa, Malik and other scholars, and they also argued with what was narrated by Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib from his father from his grandfather from Khalid ibn al-Walid that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is not permitted to eat the flesh of horses, mules and donkeys." [3] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 7/202.]]

Others said: there is no harm in eating horse meat, and there is no evidence in this verse for the prohibition of anything; rather, Allah informed His servants by this verse of His blessings upon them and alerted them to the proofs of His oneness, His lordship and the perfection of His power. To this went al-Shafi'i, and he argued with what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar and permitted the flesh of horses.

Sufyan narrated from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fed us, on the day of Khaybar, the flesh of horses, and forbade us the flesh of donkeys."

Sufyan narrated from 'Abd al-Karim from 'Ata' from Jabir, who said: "We used to eat horse meat." I said: "And mules?" He said: "No."

Hisham from 'Urwa from Fatima bint al-Mundhir from Asma' bint Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "We ate horse meat in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Sufyan from Mansur from Ibrahim said: "Our companions slaughtered a horse at al-Nakha' and ate from it, and they saw no harm in it."

"Wa-yakhluqu mā lā ta'lamūn" (And He creates what you do not know).

Some exegetes said: this means what He has prepared in Paradise for its people and in the Fire for its people, that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and which has not occurred to the heart of any human.

Qatada said: it means the weevil in garments and the worm in fruits.

Muqatil narrated from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, "wa-yakhluqu mā lā ta'lamūn," he said: He means that to the right of the Throne there is a river of light like the seven heavens, the seven earths and the seven seas. Jibril enters it every dawn and bathes, and his light increases upon his light, his beauty upon his beauty, and his greatness upon his greatness. Then he shakes himself, and from every drop that falls from his feathers Allah creates so many thousands of angels; of them, seventy thousand enter the House that is frequented (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) every day, and seventy thousand in the Ka'ba, and they do not return to it until the Hour arises.

"Wa-'alā Allāhi qaṣdu al-sabīl" (And upon Allah is the direction of the way): meaning the path of truth for you. "Al-qaṣd" is the straight path; it was also said: "'alā Allāhi al-qaṣd bikum ilā al-dīn" (upon Allah is the guiding of you to the religion). "Wa-minhā jā'irun" (and of it is that which deviates): meaning of the way is that which deviates from uprightness, crooked. It is feminine for the sake of the pronoun, because the word "sabīl" is singular while its meaning is plural; "sabīl" is feminine in the dialect of the Hijaz. The "qaṣd" of the way is the upright religion of Islam (al-Hanifiyya), and the "jā'ir" among them is Judaism, Christianity and other sects and disbelievers.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Qaṣd al-sabīl" means the explanation of the laws and obligations. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Qaṣd al-sabīl" is the Sunna, and "wa-minhā jā'irun" means the whims and innovations. Its explanation is His saying: "wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mustaqīman" (and that this is My straight path) [[Surah al-An'am: 153.]], to the end of the verse. In the codex of 'Abd Allah it reads: "wa-minkum jā'ir" (and among you is one who deviates).

"Wa-law shā'a la-hadākum ajma'īn" (And had He willed, He would have guided you all). Its parallels are His saying: "wa-law shā'a rabbuka la-āmana man fī al-arḍi kulluhum jamī'an" (Had your Lord willed, all who are on earth would have believed together) [[Surah Yunus: 99.]], and His saying: "wa-law shi'nā la-ātaynā kulla nafsin hudāhā" (Had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance) [[Surah al-Sajda: 13.]].

Some said: it is the Hour (the Final Hour).

Then Allah revealed: "Atā amr Allāh" [[Surah al-Nahl: 1.]]. The Prophet (ﷺ) leapt up, and the people raised their heads. Then it was revealed: "fa-la tasta'jilūhu" (so do not seek to hasten it), and they were reassured. "Subhanahu wa-ta'ala 'amma yushrikun" (Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him).

"Yunazzilu al-mala'ikata" (He sends down the angels).

'Ata' said: with prophethood, "fitrah" (natural disposition); the Spirit meets from His command.

Qatada: with mercy.

Abu 'Ubayda: "bi-l-rūh" means "with the Spirit," that is, with Jibril.

It is in the accusative position by the falling of the warning upon it.

"lā ilāha illā anā fa-ttaqūni" (There is no god but I, so fear Me). "Khalaqa al-samawāti wa-al-arda bi-l-haqq, ta'ala 'amma yushrikun." "Khalaqa al-insāna min nutfatin fa-idhā huwa khasīmun mubīn" (He created man from a drop, and behold he becomes an open adversary who disputes with falsehood). Its parallel is His saying: "wa-la takun li-l-khā'inīna khasīman" (and do not be an advocate for the treacherous) [[Surah al-Nisa': 105.]]. This verse was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi when he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone and said: "O Muhammad, do you think Allah will revive this after it has decayed?" Its parallel is His saying: "awa lam yara al-insānu annā khalaqnāhu min nutfatin" (Does not man see that We created him from a drop) [[Surah Ya-Sin: 77.]] to the end of the surah, also revealed about this incident.

"wa-al-an'āma khalaqahā" (And the cattle, He created them): meaning camels, cows and sheep. "Lakum fīhā difʼun" (For you in them is warmth): meaning from their wool, fleece and hair are garments, coverings and cotton, by which they keep warm. "Wa-manāfiʻu" (and benefits): in offspring, milk, riding, carrying and other things. "Wa-minhā ta'kulūn" (and from them you eat): meaning their flesh. "Wa-lakum fīhā jamālun ḥīna turīḥūn" (And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home): meaning when they are brought back in the evening from their pastures to their resting places where they take shelter. It is said: "arāḥa fulān māshiyatahu yurīḥuhā īrāḥatan," and the place to which they are brought back is "mirāḥ."

"Wa-ḥīna tasrahūn" (and when you send them out to pasture): meaning they are driven out in the morning from their pastures to their grazing grounds. It is said: "sarraḥa māshiyatahu yusarriḥuhā sarḥan wa-surūḥan" when he sent it out to graze, and "sarahat al-māshiyatu surūḥan" when it grazed.

Qatada said: That is most wondrous when they return with their udders full and their humps tall.

"Wa-tahmilu athqālakum ilā baladin ākhara lam takūnū bāligīhi illā bi-shiqqi al-anfus" (And they carry your loads to a land you would not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves).

Ikrima: "al-balad" means Makka.

The majority read "bi-shiqq" with a kasra on the shin, which has two meanings: first, hardship and difficulty; second, half, meaning you would not have reached it except with half the strength of your selves and with the other half of your strength gone.

Abu Ja'far read "bi-shaqqi" with a fatha on the shin. Both are dialect forms, like "baraqa" and "bariqa," "Ḥaṣun" and "Ḥaṣin," "raṭl" and "riṭl."

And the verse of al-Namir ibn Taulab is recited with a kasra on the shin:
"Wa-dhī ibilin yas'ā wa-yaḥsibuhā lahu... akhī naṣabin min shiqqihā wa-du'ūb"
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/184.]]

It may also be a verbal noun from "shaqaqtu 'alayhi yashuqqu shaqqan" (I burdened him).

"Inna rabbakum la-ra'ūfun raḥīm" (Indeed your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful) to His creation, in that He created these things for them and prepared for them these benefits and conveniences.

"Wa-al-khayla wa-al-bighāla wa-al-ḥamīra li-tarkabūhā wa-zīnatan" (And horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment): meaning He created them and made them an adornment along with the benefits in them.

[3] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 7/202.]]

Others said: there is no harm in eating horse meat, and there is no evidence in this verse for the prohibition of anything; rather, Allah informed His servants by this verse of His blessings upon them and alerted them to the proofs of His oneness, His lordship and the perfection of His power. To this went al-Shafi'i, and he argued with what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar and permitted the flesh of horses.

Sufyan narrated from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fed us, on the day of Khaybar, the flesh of horses, and forbade us the flesh of donkeys."

Sufyan narrated from 'Abd al-Karim from 'Ata' from Jabir, who said: "We used to eat horse meat." I said: "And mules?" He said: "No."

Hisham from 'Urwa from Fatima bint al-Mundhir from Asma' bint Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "We ate horse meat in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Sufyan from Mansur from Ibrahim said: "Our companions slaughtered a horse at al-Nakha' and ate from it, and they saw no harm in it."

Qatada said: it means the weevil in garments and the worm in fruits.

"Wa-'alā Allāhi qaṣdu al-sabīl" (And upon Allah is the direction of the way): meaning the path of truth for you. "Wa-law shā'a la-hadākum ajma'īn" (And had He willed, He would have guided you all). Qatada said: That is most wondrous when they return with their udders full and their humps tall.

"Wa-tahmilu athqālakum ilā baladin ākhara lam takūnū bāligīhi illā bi-shiqqi al-anfus" (And they carry your loads to a land you would not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves).

Ikrima: "al-balad" means Makka.

The majority read "bi-shiqq" with a kasra on the shin, which has two meanings: first, hardship and difficulty; second, half, meaning you would not have reached it except with half the strength of your selves and with the other half of your strength gone.

Abu Ja'far read "bi-shaqqi" with a fatha on the shin. Both are dialect forms, like "baraqa" and "bariqa," "Ḥaṣun" and "Ḥaṣin," "raṭl" and "riṭl."

And the verse of al-Namir ibn Taulab is recited with a kasra on the shin:
"Wa-dhī ibilin yas'ā wa-yaḥsibuhā lahu... akhī naṣabin min shiqqihā wa-du'ūb"
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/184.]]

It may also be a verbal noun from "shaqaqtu 'alayhi yashuqqu shaqqan" (I burdened him).

"Inna rabbakum la-ra'ūfun raḥīm" (Indeed your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful) to His creation, in that He created these things for them and prepared for them these benefits and conveniences.

When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his two fingers, "except that it may outrun me." [2] [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 187.]]

Ibn 'Abbas also said: The sending of the Prophet (ﷺ) was among the signs of the Hour. When Jibril passed by the people of the heavens, sent to Muhammad (ﷺ), they said: "Allahu akbar, the Hour has come."

Others said: the "amr" here is the punishment by the sword, and this is a reply to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith when he said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You..." [[Surah al-Anfal: 32.]] (to the end of the verse), seeking to hasten the punishment; so Allah revealed this verse. This is an answer in brief: al-Nadr was killed at Badr by being executed in cold blood.

Al-Dahhak said: "Amr Allah" means the rulings, the limits (hudud), and the obligations (fara'id).

The first view is more correct, because it has not reached us that any of the Companions were hasty for an obligation of Allah before it was imposed upon them, whereas those who hastened the punishment among the polytheists were many.

"Subhanahu wa-ta'ala 'amma yushrikun" (Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him).

"Yunazzilu al-mala'ikata" (He sends down the angels).

The majority of readers read it with a damma on the yaa' and a kasra on the zay with a shadda, and "al-mala'ika" in the accusative. Most people of Makka and Basra lightened it, meaning "yunzilu Allah" (Allah sends down).

Al-Mufaddal, Rawh, Suhayl and Zayd read "yanzalu" with a fatha on the yaa' and the zay, and "al-mala'ikatu" in the nominative.

Al-A'mash read "yanzilu" with a fatha on the yaa', a jazm on the nun, and a kasra on the zay, from "nuzul" (descending), and "al-mala'ikatu" in the nominative. On both of these readings the verb belongs to the angels.

"bi-l-rūh" (with the Spirit): with the revelation (wahy); he named it a spirit because hearts live by it and truth lives by it, and disbelief and falsehood die by it.

'Ata' said: with prophethood, "fitrah" (natural disposition); the Spirit meets from His command.

Qatada: with mercy.

Abu 'Ubayda: "bi-l-rūh" means "with the Spirit," that is, with Jibril.

"min amrihi 'alā man yashā'u min 'ibādihi an" (from His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, that): its position is accusative by removal of the preposition, and its sense is "bi-anna" (that), "andhirū" meaning "a'lamū" (make known), from their saying "andhir bihi" (warn him/inform him of it). It is in the accusative position by the falling of the warning upon it.

"lā ilāha illā anā fa-ttaqūni" (There is no god but I, so fear Me). "Khalaqa al-samawāti wa-al-arda bi-l-haqq, ta'ala 'amma yushrikun." "Khalaqa al-insāna min nutfatin fa-idhā huwa khasīmun mubīn" (He created man from a drop, and behold he becomes an open adversary who disputes with falsehood). Its parallel is His saying: "wa-la takun li-l-khā'inīna khasīman" (and do not be an advocate for the treacherous) [[Surah al-Nisa': 105.]]. This verse was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi when he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone and said: "O Muhammad, do you think Allah will revive this after it has decayed?" Its parallel is His saying: "awa lam yara al-insānu annā khalaqnāhu min nutfatin" (Does not man see that We created him from a drop) [[Surah Ya-Sin: 77.]] to the end of the surah, also revealed about this incident.

"wa-al-an'āma khalaqahā" (And the cattle, He created them): meaning camels, cows and sheep. "Lakum fīhā difʼun" (For you in them is warmth): meaning from their wool, fleece and hair are garments, coverings and cotton, by which they keep warm. "Wa-manāfiʻu" (and benefits): in offspring, milk, riding, carrying and other things. "Wa-minhā ta'kulūn" (and from them you eat): meaning their flesh. "Wa-lakum fīhā jamālun ḥīna turīḥūn" (And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home): meaning when they are brought back in the evening from their pastures to their resting places where they take shelter. It is said: "arāḥa fulān māshiyatahu yurīḥuhā īrāḥatan," and the place to which they are brought back is "mirāḥ."

"Wa-ḥīna tasrahūn" (and when you send them out to pasture): meaning they are driven out in the morning from their pastures to their grazing grounds. It is said: "sarraḥa māshiyatahu yusarriḥuhā sarḥan wa-surūḥan" when he sent it out to graze, and "sarahat al-māshiyatu surūḥan" when it grazed.

Qatada said: That is most wondrous when they return with their udders full and their humps tall.

"Wa-tahmilu athqālakum ilā baladin ākhara lam takūnū bāligīhi illā bi-shiqqi al-anfus" (And they carry your loads to a land you would not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves).

Ikrima: "al-balad" means Makka.

The majority read "bi-shiqq" with a kasra on the shin, which has two meanings: first, hardship and difficulty; second, half, meaning you would not have reached it except with half the strength of your selves and with the other half of your strength gone.

Abu Ja'far read "bi-shaqqi" with a fatha on the shin. Both are dialect forms, like "baraqa" and "bariqa," "Ḥaṣun" and "Ḥaṣin," "raṭl" and "riṭl."

And the verse of al-Namir ibn Taulab is recited with a kasra on the shin:
"Wa-dhī ibilin yas'ā wa-yaḥsibuhā lahu... akhī naṣabin min shiqqihā wa-du'ūb"
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/184.]]

It may also be a verbal noun from "shaqaqtu 'alayhi yashuqqu shaqqan" (I burdened him).

"Inna rabbakum la-ra'ūfun raḥīm" (Indeed your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful) to His creation, in that He created these things for them and prepared for them these benefits and conveniences.

"Wa-al-khayla wa-al-bighāla wa-al-ḥamīra li-tarkabūhā wa-zīnatan" (And horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment): meaning He created them and made them an adornment along with the benefits in them.

Some jurists used this verse as evidence for the prohibition of eating horse meat. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about eating horse meat, and he disliked it, and recited this verse: "wa-al-khayla wa-al-bighāla wa-al-ḥamīra li-tarkabūhā wa-zīnatan."

He said: "It is for riding." He recited the preceding verse, "wa-al-an'āma khalaqahā" etc., and said: "That is for eating."

He said: "The ruling on eating horse meat is prohibited in the Book of Allah," then he recited these verses and said: "He made these for eating and those for riding."

To this view went Abu Hanifa, Malik and other scholars, and they also argued with what was narrated by Salih ibn Yahya ibn al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib from his father from his grandfather from Khalid ibn al-Walid that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is not permitted to eat the flesh of horses, mules and donkeys." [3] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 7/202.]]

Others said: there is no harm in eating horse meat, and there is no evidence in this verse for the prohibition of anything; rather, Allah informed His servants by this verse of His blessings upon them and alerted them to the proofs of His oneness, His lordship and the perfection of His power. To this went al-Shafi'i, and he argued with what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar and permitted the flesh of horses.

Sufyan narrated from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fed us, on the day of Khaybar, the flesh of horses, and forbade us the flesh of donkeys."

Sufyan narrated from 'Abd al-Karim from 'Ata' from Jabir, who said: "We used to eat horse meat." I said: "And mules?" He said: "No."

Hisham from 'Urwa from Fatima bint al-Mundhir from Asma' bint Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "We ate horse meat in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Sufyan from Mansur from Ibrahim said: "Our companions slaughtered a horse at al-Nakha' and ate from it, and they saw no harm in it."

"Wa-yakhluqu mā lā ta'lamūn" (And He creates what you do not know).

Some exegetes said: this means what He has prepared in Paradise for its people and in the Fire for its people, that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and which has not occurred to the heart of any human.

Qatada said: it means the weevil in garments and the worm in fruits.

Muqatil narrated from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, "wa-yakhluqu mā lā ta'lamūn," he said: He means that to the right of the Throne there is a river of light like the seven heavens, the seven earths and the seven seas. Jibril enters it every dawn and bathes, and his light increases upon his light, his beauty upon his beauty, and his greatness upon his greatness. Then he shakes himself, and from every drop that falls from his feathers Allah creates so many thousands of angels; of them, seventy thousand enter the House that is frequented (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) every day, and seventy thousand in the Ka'ba, and they do not return to it until the Hour arises.

"Wa-'alā Allāhi qaṣdu al-sabīl" (And upon Allah is the direction of the way): meaning the path of truth for you. "Al-qaṣd" is the straight path; it was also said: "'alā Allāhi al-qaṣd bikum ilā al-dīn" (upon Allah is the guiding of you to the religion). "Wa-minhā jā'irun" (and of it is that which deviates): meaning of the way is that which deviates from uprightness, crooked. It is feminine for the sake of the pronoun, because the word "sabīl" is singular while its meaning is plural; "sabīl" is feminine in the dialect of the Hijaz. The "qaṣd" of the way is the upright religion of Islam (al-Hanifiyya), and the "jā'ir" among them is Judaism, Christianity and other sects and disbelievers.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Qaṣd al-sabīl" means the explanation of the laws and obligations. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Qaṣd al-sabīl" is the Sunna, and "wa-minhā jā'irun" means the whims and innovations. Its explanation is His saying: "wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mustaqīman" (and that this is My straight path) [[Surah al-An'am: 153.]], to the end of the verse. In the codex of 'Abd Allah it reads: "wa-minkum jā'ir" (and among you is one who deviates).

"Wa-law shā'a la-hadākum ajma'īn" (And had He willed, He would have guided you all). Its parallels are His saying: "wa-law shā'a rabbuka la-āmana man fī al-arḍi kulluhum jamī'an" (Had your Lord willed, all who are on earth would have believed together) [[Surah Yunus: 99.]], and His saying: "wa-law shi'nā la-ātaynā kulla nafsin hudāhā" (Had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance) [[Surah al-Sajda: 13.]].

It is He who sent down water from the sky; from it is drink for you, and from it is [growth of] trees upon which you pasture [your livestock]. (Q. 16:10)

[Tha'alabi, commentary:] "Minhu shajar" — i.e., from that water is what grows as trees, which are your saplings, your life, your plantings, and your growth. "Fihi" — in it, in the tree; it is a general noun (ism 'amm) [[as in the original manuscript]]. He used the pronoun because He returned it to the word shajar (tree).

"Tusimun" means you pasture [your livestock]. "Wa-yunbitu lakum" ... Asama fulan ibilahu yusimuha isamatan means: he pastured his camels; so he is musim, and they are sa'ima, pasturing (yasumu).

The poet said:

"The people walked with the litters toward the pasture, and the one who pastured [the herd] grew weary of the long drive."

That is, they bring the litters down beneath the bellies of the pasturing [camels]. [...] [[illegible words in the manuscript]].

The poet said:

"Woe to you, son of the pasturing mother of camels."

That is: O son of the shepherdess of camels.

"Yunbitu lakum" — the common readers recite it with the ya' (yunbitu), meaning: He causes to grow for you. 'Asim, by the transmission of al-Mufaddal, Hammad and Yahya, recited it with the nun (nunbitu), and the first is the preferred reading.

By it, by the water which He sent down, [He causes to grow] the crops, the olives, the date palms, the grapes, and fruits of every kind. Surely in that is a sign for a people who reflect.

"And He subjected for you the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command." The common readers recite "wa-l-nujumu musakhkharatun" in the accusative (nasb), coordinating it with what precedes. Hafs, on the authority of 'Asim, recited "wa-l-nujumu musakhkharatun" with the nominative (raf'), as predicate and subject. Ibn 'Amir recited "wa-l-shamsu wa-l-qamaru wa-l-nujumu musakhkharatun" all in the nominative, as subject and predicate.

"Bi-amrihi" — by His permission. "Surely in that are signs for a people who understand."

"Wa-ma dhara'a" — meaning: and He subjected what He created for your sake, from animals, trees, fruits and other things, in the earth, varied in its colours. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

Surely in that is a sign for a people who remember.

It is He who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh flesh, meaning fish, and extract from it ornaments, meaning pearls and coral.

Hammad ibn Yahya narrated from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: A man came to Ibn Ja'far and said: Is there zakat on women's ornaments? He said: No; they are as Allah said: "ornaments that you wear."

"You wear them, and you see the ships ploughing through it."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "jawari" (running).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "mu'tarida" (crossing). Qatadah and Muqatil: [they go and come] coming and going, with one wind.

Al-Hasan: "mawaqir" (laden).

'Ikrimah, al-Farra' and al-Akhfash: splitting, cleaving the water with their prows.

Mujahid: the ships plough (yamkhuru) the water with the winds; and no one ploughs the wind from the ships except a great king.

Abu 'Ubaydah: "sawabih" (gliding).

The origin of al-makhr is pushing and cleaving, from which comes makhr al-ard (the ploughing of the earth). It is said: "imtakhara al-rih" and "tamakhkharaha," when one looks to see from where the wind is blowing.

In a hadith: "When one of you wishes to urinate, let him check the direction of the wind," i.e., let him look where it blows from and face away from it, so that the urine does not splash back on him.

"And that you may seek of His bounty," meaning trade, "and perhaps you will be grateful."

"And He placed in the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you," meaning lest it shake with you, i.e., move and tilt. Al-maid is agitation and imbalance, and from it the dizziness that overtakes sea travellers is called "mayd."

Wahb said: When Allah created the earth, it began to shake and sway. The angels said: This will not let anyone stand upon its back. So it was made fast with mountains, and the angels did not know what the mountains were created from.

'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When Allah created the earth, it refused and said: "O Lord, will You place upon me the children of Adam, who will commit sin upon me and cast filth upon me?" So Allah set in it mountains, what you see and what you do not see.

"And rivers" — meaning He placed in it rivers; "and roads," different paths, "that perhaps you may be guided"; "and landmarks," so that you do not go astray or become bewildered, meaning landmarks of the ways.

Some said: Here the speech ends, and then a new statement begins: "And by the star they are guided."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Kalbi said: By the landmarks He meant the mountains; the mountains are landmarks by day, and the stars are landmarks by night.

Mujahid and Ibrahim said: By both of them they meant the stars, some of which are landmarks and some by which they are guided.

Al-Suddi said: He meant by them the Pleiades, the Great and Little Bear, the two Guards [of the pole] and the Pole Star, by which they are guided to the roads and the qibla.

Qatadah: Allah created the stars for three things: as an adornment of the sky, as landmarks for the way, and as missiles against the devils. Whoever says other than this has spoken by his own opinion and burdened himself with what he has no knowledge of.

"Is He who creates [Allah, the Exalted] like one who creates not [the idols]? Will you not then remember?" Its parallel is His saying: "This is the creation of Allah; show me what those besides Him have created" (Q. 31:11), and His saying: "Show me what they have created of the earth" (Q. 35:40).

"And if you should count Allah's favours, you could not enumerate them. Surely Allah is Forgiving of what you did of shortcoming in thanking His favours, Merciful to you, in that He has widened His favours upon you and did not cut them off because of your shortcomings and disobedience. Allah knows what you conceal and what you disclose."

By it, by the water which He sent down, [He causes to grow] the crops, the olives, the date palms, the grapes, and fruits of every kind. Surely in that is a sign for a people who reflect.

"And He subjected for you the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command." The common readers recite "wa-l-nujumu musakhkharatun" in the accusative (nasb), coordinating it with what precedes. Hafs, on the authority of 'Asim, recited "wa-l-nujumu musakhkharatun" with the nominative (raf'), as predicate and subject. Ibn 'Amir recited "wa-l-shamsu wa-l-qamaru wa-l-nujumu musakhkharatun" all in the nominative, as subject and predicate.

"Bi-amrihi" — by His permission. "Surely in that are signs for a people who understand."

"Wa-ma dhara'a" — meaning: and He subjected what He created for your sake, from animals, trees, fruits and other things, in the earth, varied in its colours. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

Surely in that is a sign for a people who remember.

It is He who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh flesh, meaning fish, and extract from it ornaments, meaning pearls and coral.

Hammad ibn Yahya narrated from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: A man came to Ibn Ja'far and said: Is there zakat on women's ornaments? He said: No; they are as Allah said: "ornaments that you wear."

"You wear them, and you see the ships ploughing through it."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "jawari" (running).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "mu'tarida" (crossing). Qatadah and Muqatil: [they go and come] coming and going, with one wind.

Al-Hasan: "mawaqir" (laden).

'Ikrimah, al-Farra' and al-Akhfash: splitting, cleaving the water with their prows.

Mujahid: the ships plough (yamkhuru) the water with the winds; and no one ploughs the wind from the ships except a great king.

Abu 'Ubaydah: "sawabih" (gliding).

The origin of al-makhr is pushing and cleaving, from which comes makhr al-ard (the ploughing of the earth). It is said: "imtakhara al-rih" and "tamakhkharaha," when one looks to see from where the wind is blowing.

In a hadith: "When one of you wishes to urinate, let him check the direction of the wind," i.e., let him look where it blows from and face away from it, so that the urine does not splash back on him.

"And that you may seek of His bounty," meaning trade, "and perhaps you will be grateful."

"And He placed in the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you," meaning lest it shake with you, i.e., move and tilt. Al-maid is agitation and imbalance, and from it the dizziness that overtakes sea travellers is called "mayd."

Wahb said: When Allah created the earth, it began to shake and sway. The angels said: This will not let anyone stand upon its back. So it was made fast with mountains, and the angels did not know what the mountains were created from.

'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When Allah created the earth, it refused and said: "O Lord, will You place upon me the children of Adam, who will commit sin upon me and cast filth upon me?" So Allah set in it mountains, what you see and what you do not see.

"And rivers" — meaning He placed in it rivers; "and roads," different paths, "that perhaps you may be guided"; "and landmarks," so that you do not go astray or become bewildered, meaning landmarks of the ways.

Some said: Here the speech ends, and then a new statement begins: "And by the star they are guided."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Kalbi said: By the landmarks He meant the mountains; the mountains are landmarks by day, and the stars are landmarks by night.

Mujahid and Ibrahim said: By both of them they meant the stars, some of which are landmarks and some by which they are guided.

Al-Suddi said: He meant by them the Pleiades, the Great and Little Bear, the two Guards [of the pole] and the Pole Star, by which they are guided to the roads and the qibla.

Qatadah: Allah created the stars for three things: as an adornment of the sky, as landmarks for the way, and as missiles against the devils. Whoever says other than this has spoken by his own opinion and burdened himself with what he has no knowledge of.

"Is He who creates [Allah, the Exalted] like one who creates not [the idols]? Will you not then remember?" Its parallel is His saying: "This is the creation of Allah; show me what those besides Him have created" (Q. 31:11), and His saying: "Show me what they have created of the earth" (Q. 35:40).

Surely Allah is Forgiving of what you did of shortcoming in thanking His favours, Merciful to you, in that He has widened His favours upon you and did not cut them off because of your shortcomings and disobedience. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 16, verse 20–29:

وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ.

"Those whom they call upon besides Allah" (﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾).

The majority (al-'ammah) read it with the taa' (تَدْعُونَ), because what precedes it is all addressed in the second person (khitab).

Ya'qub, 'Asim and Sahl read it with the yaa' (يَدْعُونَ).

﴿لا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئاً وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ﴾ ("They create nothing, while they themselves are created"). Then he described the idols, saying: ﴿أَمْواتٌ﴾ ("They are dead"), meaning they are dead, ﴿غَيْرُ أَحْياءٍ﴾ ("not living"), and ﴿وَما يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ("and they do not perceive"), meaning the idols. ﴿أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ ("when they will be raised") — he referred to them in the way he referred to human beings, [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/94, adding: "because they claimed that they understand on their behalf, know, and intercede for them with Allah the Exalted, so their address followed that belief," and he did not attribute it to the author, as is his custom.]] and this matter has already passed. It is also said: "And the disbelievers who worship idols do not know when they will be raised."

﴿إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ﴾ ("Your God is one God"). ﴿فَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مُنْكِرَةٌ﴾ ("As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are denying"), meaning defiant, disbelieving, not recognizing. ﴿وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and they are arrogant"), meaning self-magnifying. ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ ("Assuredly"), meaning truly. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ﴾ ("that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant"). ﴿وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ ("And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?'"), ﴿قالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("They say, 'Tales of the ancients'").

It means: when it is said to those who do not believe in the Hereafter, namely the idolaters of Quraysh who divided up the passes of Makkah and its gates, the pilgrims and delegations during the season of pilgrimage asked them about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what was revealed to him, and they said: ﴿أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, meaning their tales and falsehoods.

﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزارَهُمْ﴾ ("So that they may bear their own burdens"), meaning the sins of themselves in which they persist, ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ ("and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge"), who turn them away from faith. ﴿أَلا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ﴾ ("Unquestionably, evil is what they bear"), meaning evil is the burden they carry. Its parallel is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ﴾ ("And they will surely bear their burdens") [[Surah al-'Ankabut: 13]], and so on.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to misguidance and is followed, he will have the like of the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything of their sins. And whoever calls to guidance and is followed, he will have the like of their rewards, without that diminishing anything of their rewards." [4] [[Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/466, no. 3010.]]

﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ ("Those before them had already schemed"). This refers to Nimrod ibn Kan'an when he built the tower (al-sarh) in Babylon, and it was necessary from it to ascend to the sky to look and to claim (to see) the God of Abraham. This story has already passed.

Ibn 'Abbas and Wahb said: the height of the tower in the sky was five thousand cubits.

Ka'b and Muqatil said: its height was two farsakhs. Then a wind blew and cast its top into the sea, and the rest of it fell upon them, their houses were torn apart, and Nimrod was overwhelmed. When the tower collapsed, people's tongues were confused (tabalbalat) from the terror, so they spoke seventy-three languages, and for this reason it was named Babel (Babil). Before that, the people's language had been Syriac. This is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿فَأَتَى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَواعِدِ﴾ ("So Allah came upon their structure from its foundations"), meaning He aimed to destroy their building from its roots. ﴿فَأَتاها أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ ("Then the command of Allah came upon it"), which is the wind that destroyed it. ﴿فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ ("So the roof fell upon them from above them"), meaning the upper parts of the houses. ﴿وَأَتاهُمُ الْعَذابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ("And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive"), from their place of safety. ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ﴾ ("Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them"), humiliating them with punishment. ﴿وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾ ("And He will say, 'Where are My partners about whom you used to oppose'"), meaning you used to form alliances concerning them, ﴿لا ينقذونكم فيدفعوا عنكم العذاب﴾ — they will not save you so as to avert the punishment from you.

The majority read ﴿تُشَاقُّونَ﴾ with a fatha on the nun, except Nafi', who read it with a kasra as an annexed form (al-idafah). ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ ("Those who were given knowledge will say"), meaning the believers: ﴿إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ الْيَوْمَ وَالسُّوءَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ ("Indeed, disgrace today and evil are upon the disbelievers"), meaning the punishment. ﴿الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ ("Those whom the angels take in death"), meaning the angels take their souls, the angel of death and his assistants. ﴿ظالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("while they are wronging themselves") by disbelief, a circumstantial accusative (nasb 'ala al-hal), meaning in the state of their disbelief. ﴿فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ﴾ ("Then they will surrender"), meaning they submitted and yielded, and said: ﴿ما كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍ﴾ ("We were not doing any evil"), meaning polytheism. The angels said to them: ﴿بَلى إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("Yes, indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do").

'Ikrimah said: this refers to those of Quraysh and the people of Makkah who were killed at Badr, and who had been brought out there under compulsion.

﴿فَادْخُلُوا أَبْوابَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها فَلَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ ("So enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant") — those who were arrogant toward faith.

Then he described the idols, saying: ﴿أَمْواتٌ﴾ ("They are dead"), meaning they are dead, ﴿غَيْرُ أَحْياءٍ﴾ ("not living"), and ﴿وَما يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ("and they do not perceive"), meaning the idols. ﴿أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ ("when they will be raised") — he referred to them in the way he referred to human beings, [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/94, adding: "because they claimed that they understand on their behalf, know, and intercede for them with Allah the Exalted, so their address followed that belief," and he did not attribute it to the author, as is his custom.]] and this matter has already passed. It is also said: "And the disbelievers who worship idols do not know when they will be raised."

﴿إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ﴾ ("Your God is one God"). ﴿فَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مُنْكِرَةٌ﴾ ("As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are denying"), meaning defiant, disbelieving, not recognizing. ﴿وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("and they are arrogant"), meaning self-magnifying. ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ ("Assuredly"), meaning truly. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ﴾ ("that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant"). ﴿وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ ("And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?'"), ﴿قالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("They say, 'Tales of the ancients'").

It means: when it is said to those who do not believe in the Hereafter, namely the idolaters of Quraysh who divided up the passes of Makkah and its gates, the pilgrims and delegations during the season of pilgrimage asked them about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what was revealed to him, and they said: ﴿أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, meaning their tales and falsehoods.

﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزارَهُمْ﴾ ("So that they may bear their own burdens"), meaning the sins of themselves in which they persist, ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ ("and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge"), who turn them away from faith. ﴿أَلا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ﴾ ("Unquestionably, evil is what they bear"), meaning evil is the burden they carry. Its parallel is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ﴾ ("And they will surely bear their burdens") [[Surah al-'Ankabut: 13]], and so on.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to misguidance and is followed, he will have the like of the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything of their sins. And whoever calls to guidance and is followed, he will have the like of their rewards, without that diminishing anything of their rewards." [4] [[Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/466, no. 3010.]]

﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ ("Those before them had already schemed"). This refers to Nimrod ibn Kan'an when he built the tower (al-sarh) in Babylon, and it was necessary from it to ascend to the sky to look and to claim (to see) the God of Abraham. This story has already passed.

Ibn 'Abbas and Wahb said: the height of the tower in the sky was five thousand cubits.

Ka'b and Muqatil said: its height was two farsakhs. Then a wind blew and cast its top into the sea, and the rest of it fell upon them, their houses were torn apart, and Nimrod was overwhelmed. When the tower collapsed, people's tongues were confused (tabalbalat) from the terror, so they spoke seventy-three languages, and for this reason it was named Babel (Babil). Before that, the people's language had been Syriac. This is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿فَأَتَى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَواعِدِ﴾ ("So Allah came upon their structure from its foundations"), meaning He aimed to destroy their building from its roots. ﴿فَأَتاها أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ ("Then the command of Allah came upon it"), which is the wind that destroyed it. ﴿فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ ("So the roof fell upon them from above them"), meaning the upper parts of the houses. ﴿وَأَتاهُمُ الْعَذابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ("And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive"), from their place of safety. ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ﴾ ("Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them"), humiliating them with punishment. ﴿وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾ ("And He will say, 'Where are My partners about whom you used to oppose'"), meaning you used to form alliances concerning them, ﴿لا ينقذونكم فيدفعوا عنكم العذاب﴾ — they will not save you so as to avert the punishment from you.

The majority read ﴿تُشَاقُّونَ﴾ with a fatha on the nun, except Nafi', who read it with a kasra as an annexed form (al-idafah). ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ ("Those who were given knowledge will say"), meaning the believers: ﴿إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ الْيَوْمَ وَالسُّوءَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ ("Indeed, disgrace today and evil are upon the disbelievers"), meaning the punishment. ﴿الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ ("Those whom the angels take in death"), meaning the angels take their souls, the angel of death and his assistants. ﴿ظالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("while they are wronging themselves") by disbelief, a circumstantial accusative (nasb 'ala al-hal), meaning in the state of their disbelief. ﴿فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ﴾ ("Then they will surrender"), meaning they submitted and yielded, and said: ﴿ما كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍ﴾ ("We were not doing any evil"), meaning polytheism. The angels said to them: ﴿بَلى إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("Yes, indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do").

'Ikrimah said: this refers to those of Quraysh and the people of Makkah who were killed at Badr, and who had been brought out there under compulsion.

﴿فَادْخُلُوا أَبْوابَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها فَلَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ ("So enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant") — those who were arrogant toward faith.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 16, verses 30–34:**

﴿And it is said to those who were mindful of God: "What has your Lord sent down?" They say: "Good."﴾ This is because the tribes of the Arabs used to send, during the season (of pilgrimage), someone who would bring them news of the Prophet ﷺ. When he came, he would ask those who sat along the roads about him, and they would say: "A poet, a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a liar, a madman" [and it divides brothers] [[The manuscript is confused, and what we have recorded is the apparent reading.]]. They would say: "If you do not meet him, it is better for you." The questioner would say: "I would be the worst of the worst if I returned to my people without entering Makkah and investigating the matter of Muhammad, or meeting him." So he would enter Makkah, see the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they would inform him of his truthfulness and that he was a prophet sent (by God). This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is said to those who were mindful of God: "What has your Lord sent down?" They say: "Good."﴾

If it is asked: Why is the answer of the polytheists raised in their saying ﴿Tales of the ancients﴾ (أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ), while it is put in the accusative in His saying ﴿Good﴾ (خَيْرًا)?

The answer: The polytheists did not believe in the revelation, so when they were asked, they said: "Tales of the ancients" (أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ), meaning that what Muhammad ﷺ says is the tales of the ancients. The believers, however, were affirming the revelation, so when they were asked: ﴿What has your Lord sent down?﴾ they said: "Good" (خَيْرًا), meaning: He sent down good.

Then (God) began (a new statement) and said: ﴿For those who did good in this world there is a good (reward)﴾, a generosity from God. ﴿And the Abode of the Hereafter is better, and excellent is the abode of those who are mindful (of God).﴾ Then He explained it, saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden which they will enter﴾, as a substitution for "the abode" (الدار), which is why it is in the nominative. ﴿Beneath them rivers flow; for them therein is whatever they wish. Thus does God reward those who are mindful (of Him).﴾ ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure﴾, meaning believers. Mujahid said: their deeds and their words are pure.

﴿They say﴾, meaning in the verse: ﴿Peace be upon you. Enter the Garden for what you used to do.﴾

Al-Qurazi said: When the soul of the believing servant is about to depart, the Angel of Death comes to him and says: "Peace be upon you, friend of God. God sends you His greetings and gives you the glad tidings of Paradise."

﴿Do they await only that the angels come to them﴾, meaning to take their souls.

﴿Or that the command of your Lord comes?﴾ meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the punishment.

﴿So did those before them. And God did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves. So the evils of what they had done afflicted them﴾, meaning the punishments of their disbelief and their corrupt deeds.

﴿And there encompassed them what they used to mock.﴾ That is, it descended upon them.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 16, verses 35–40:

وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما عَبَدْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ نَحْنُ وَلا آباؤُنا قل للذين اقتدينا بهم وَلا حَرَّمْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يعني البحيرة والسائبة والوصيلة والحام فلولا أن رضيها لغير ذلك ببعض عقوباته أو هدانا إلى غيرها.

Translation: ﴿And those who associated partners with God said: "Had God willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything without Him."﴾ He means the baḥīra (a she-camel whose ear was slit and set free), the sā'iba (a freed camel), the waṣīla (a she-camel or ewe that bore twins of the same sex), and the ḥām (a stallion camel freed after a number of offspring). So, if He had been pleased with something else, He would have punished them with some of His punishments, or He would have guided us to something else.

قال الله: كَذلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَهَلْ عَلَى الرُّسُلِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ يعني إلّا عليه، فإنّها لم تحرم هذه الأشياء وأنهم ادعوا على الله.

Translation: God said: ﴿Thus did those before them act. Is there upon the messengers anything but clear conveyance?﴾ He means: [the messenger's duty is] only upon him, for these things were not forbidden [by God], and they were attributing [this] to God falsely.

وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ يعني بأن اعبدوا الله وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ وهو كل معبود من دون الله فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ هَدَى اللَّهُ في دينه وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ حَقَّتْ أي وجبت عَلَيْهِ الضَّلالَةُ حتّى مات على كفره فَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ أي خراب منازلهم وديارهم بالعذاب والهلاك إِنْ تَحْرِصْ يا محمّد عَلى هُداهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ.

Translation: ﴿And We certainly sent into every community a messenger: "Worship God and avoid the Ṭāghūt."﴾ He means: that you should worship God. The ṭāghūt (every object of worship besides God) is [what you must avoid]. ﴿Among them were those whom God guided in His religion, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed.﴾ That is: it became necessary for them, so that they died in their disbelief. ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ That is: the ruin of their dwellings and homes through punishment and destruction. ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, O Muhammad, then indeed God does not guide one whom He leads astray.﴾

قرأ أهل الكوفة: يَهْدِي بفتح الياء وقسموا ذلك، ولها وجهان: أحدهما: إن معناه فإنّ الله لا يهدي من أضله الله، والآخر: أن يكون يهدي بمعنى يهتدي، بمعنى من أضله الله لا يهتدي [[راجع تفسير القرطبي 10/ 104.]] يقول العرب: هدى الرجل وهم يريدون اهتدى.

Translation: The people of Kufa recited يَهْدِي with a fatḥa on the yā' (yahdī), and they divided it [into two readings]. It has two meanings. The first: that God does not guide those whom God has led astray. The second: that يَهْدِي means يَهْتَدِي (to be guided), so that the meaning is: whoever God leads astray does not become guided. The Arabs say: "The man guided (hadā)," meaning "he became guided (ihtadā)." [See al-Qurṭubi's tafsir 10/104.]

وقرأ الباقون: بضم الياء وفتح الدال، واختاره أبو عبيدة وأبو حاتم على معنى من أضله الله فلا هادي له، دليله: مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ [[سورة الأعراف: 186.]] .

Translation: The rest [of the readers] recited it with a ḍamma on the yā' and a fatḥa on the dāl (yuhdī). Abū 'Ubayda and Abū Ḥātim preferred this, with the meaning: whom God has led astray, there is no guide for him. Its evidence is ﴿Whomever God leads astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 186].

وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ يمنعونهم من عذاب الله وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ.

Translation: ﴿And they have no helpers﴾, who would protect them from the punishment of God. ﴿And they swore by God with their most emphatic oaths that God will not raise up one who dies.﴾

الربيع عن أبي العالية قال: كان لرجل من المسلمين على رجل من المشركين دين فأتاه يتقاضاه فكان فيما تكلّم به: والذي أرجوه بعد الموت أنه لكذا، فقال المشرك: وإنك لتزعم أنك تبعث بعد الموت فأقسم بالله (لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ) فأنزل الله هذه الآية.

Translation: Al-Rabi' reported from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: A man from among the Muslims had a debt owed to him by a man from among the polytheists. He came to him to demand it, and among what he said was: "By the one I hope for after death, that it is such-and-such." The polytheist said: "Do you really claim that you will be raised after death?" and swore by God: ﴿God will not raise up one who dies.﴾ Then God revealed this verse.

قتادة: ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال لابن عبّاس: إن ناسا بالعراق يزعمون أن عليا مبعوث قبل يوم القيامة ويتأولون هذه الآية.

Translation: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Some people in Iraq claim that 'Ali will be raised before the Day of Resurrection, and they interpret this verse [in support of that]."

فقال ابن عبّاس: كذب أولئك، إنما هذه الآية عامة للناس، لو كان عليّ مبعوثا قبل يوم القيامة ما نكحنا نساءه ولا قسمنا ميراثه، قال الله ردا عليهم: بَلى وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ.

Translation: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Those people are liars. This verse is general for all people. If 'Ali were raised before the Day of Resurrection, we would not have married his wives, nor divided his inheritance." God said, refuting them: ﴿Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth, but most people do not know.﴾

في الخبر أن الله تعالى يقول: كذّبني ابن آدم ولم يكن له أن يكذبني، وشتمني ابن آدم ولا ينبغي له أن يشتمني، وأمّا تكذيبه إياي فحلفه بي أن لا أبعث الخلق، وأمّا شتمه إياي فقوله اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً وأنا الله الواحد الصمد الذي لم ألد ولم أولد ولم يكن لي كُفُواً أَحَدٌ.

Translation: It is reported in a report that God, exalted is He, says: "The son of Adam has denied Me, and it was not his right to deny Me; and the son of Adam has reviled Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me. As for his denial of Me, it is his swearing by Me that I will not raise up creation; and as for his reviling of Me, it is his saying: ﴿God has taken a son﴾. But I am God, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not begotten and has not been begotten, and there is none comparable to Me."

لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ هو مردود إلى قوله: لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ بَلى وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا يبين لهؤلاء المنكرين المقتسمين الذين يختلفون وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كاذِبِينَ.

Translation: ﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾: this refers back to His saying: ﴿God will not raise up one who dies. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth.﴾ He makes clear to these deniers, the ones who divided [the oath] and differed [among themselves]. ﴿And that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.﴾

إِنَّما قَوْلُنا لِشَيْءٍ الآية، يقول الله جل ثناؤه وتقدست أسماؤه: إنا إذا أردنا أن نبعث من يموت فلا تعب علينا ولا نصب في إحيائهم ولا في غير ذلك [مما نخلق ونكون ونحدث] ، لأنا إذا أردنا خلق شيء وإنشاؤه أَنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ [[تفسير الطبري: 14/ 141.]] .

Translation: ﴿Our word to a thing, when We intend it, is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ God, majestic is His praise and sanctified are His names, says: When We intend to raise up one who has died, there is no toil upon Us nor fatigue in bringing them to life, nor in anything else [that We create, bring into being, or originate], because when We intend to create a thing and bring it into being, We only say to it, "Be," and it is. [See al-Tabari's tafsir 14/141.]

وفي هذه الآية دليل على أنّ القرآن غير مخلوق، فذكر أن الله عزّ وجلّ أخبر أنه إذا أراد شيئا قال لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ، فلو كان قوله كُنْ مخلوقا لاحتاج إلى قول ثان ولاحتاج ذلك القول إلى قول ثالث إلى ما لا نهاية فلما بطل ذلك ثبت أن الله خلق الخلق بكلام غير مخلوق.

Translation: In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is uncreated. He mentioned that God, mighty and majestic, informed that when He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is. If His saying "Be" were created, it would require a second saying, and that saying would require a third, and so on without end. Since this is impossible, it is established that God created creation through uncreated speech.

Translation: ﴿And they have no helpers﴾, who would protect them from the punishment of God. ﴿And they swore by God with their most emphatic oaths that God will not raise up one who dies.﴾

Translation: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Those people are liars. This verse is general for all people. Translation: It is reported in a report that God, exalted is He, says: "The son of Adam has denied Me, and it was not his right to deny Me; and the son of Adam has reviled Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me. لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ هو مردود إلى قوله: لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ بَلى وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا يبين لهؤلاء المنكرين المقتسمين الذين يختلفون وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كاذِبِينَ.

Translation: ﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾: this refers back to His saying: ﴿God will not raise up one who dies. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth.﴾ He makes clear to these deniers, the ones who divided [the oath] and differed [among themselves]. ﴿And that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.﴾

Translation: ﴿Our word to a thing, when We intend it, is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ God, majestic is His praise and sanctified are His names, says: When We intend to raise up one who has died, there is no toil upon Us nor fatigue in bringing them to life, nor in anything else [that We create, bring into being, or originate], because when We intend to create a thing and bring it into being, We only say to it, "Be," and it is. Translation: In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is uncreated. He mentioned that God, mighty and majestic, informed that when He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is. وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما عَبَدْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ نَحْنُ وَلا آباؤُنا قل للذين اقتدينا بهم وَلا حَرَّمْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يعني البحيرة والسائبة والوصيلة والحام فلولا أن رضيها لغير ذلك ببعض عقوباته أو هدانا إلى غيرها.

Translation: ﴿And those who associated partners with God said: "Had God willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything without Him."﴾ He means the baḥīra (a she-camel whose ear was slit and set free), the sā'iba (a freed camel), the waṣīla (a she-camel or ewe that bore twins of the same sex), and the ḥām (a stallion camel freed after a number of offspring). So, if He had been pleased with something else, He would have punished them with some of His punishments, or He would have guided us to something else.

قال الله: كَذلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَهَلْ عَلَى الرُّسُلِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ يعني إلّا عليه، فإنّها لم تحرم هذه الأشياء وأنهم ادعوا على الله.

Translation: God said: ﴿Thus did those before them act. Is there upon the messengers anything but clear conveyance?﴾ He means: [the messenger's duty is] only upon him, for these things were not forbidden [by God], and they were attributing [this] to God falsely.

وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ يعني بأن اعبدوا الله وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ وهو كل معبود من دون الله فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ هَدَى اللَّهُ في دينه وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ حَقَّتْ أي وجبت عَلَيْهِ الضَّلالَةُ حتّى مات على كفره فَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ أي خراب منازلهم وديارهم بالعذاب والهلاك إِنْ تَحْرِصْ يا محمّد عَلى هُداهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ.

Translation: ﴿And We certainly sent into every community a messenger: "Worship God and avoid the Ṭāghūt."﴾ He means: that you should worship God. The ṭāghūt (every object of worship besides God) is [what you must avoid]. ﴿Among them were those whom God guided in His religion, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed.﴾ That is: it became necessary for them, so that they died in their disbelief. ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ That is: the ruin of their dwellings and homes through punishment and destruction. ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, O Muhammad, then indeed God does not guide one whom He leads astray.﴾

قرأ أهل الكوفة: يَهْدِي بفتح الياء وقسموا ذلك، ولها وجهان: أحدهما: إن معناه فإنّ الله لا يهدي من أضله الله، والآخر: أن يكون يهدي بمعنى يهتدي، بمعنى من أضله الله لا يهتدي [[راجع تفسير القرطبي 10/ 104.]] يقول العرب: هدى الرجل وهم يريدون اهتدى.

Translation: The people of Kufa recited يَهْدِي with a fatḥa on the yā' (yahdī), and they divided it [into two readings]. It has two meanings. The first: that God does not guide those whom God has led astray. The second: that يَهْدِي means يَهْتَدِي (to be guided), so that the meaning is: whoever God leads astray does not become guided. The Arabs say: "The man guided (hadā)," meaning "he became guided (ihtadā)." [See al-Qurṭubi's tafsir 10/104.]

وقرأ الباقون: بضم الياء وفتح الدال، واختاره أبو عبيدة وأبو حاتم على معنى من أضله الله فلا هادي له، دليله: مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ [[سورة الأعراف: 186.]] .

Translation: The rest [of the readers] recited it with a ḍamma on the yā' and a fatḥa on the dāl (yuhdī). Abū 'Ubayda and Abū Ḥātim preferred this, with the meaning: whom God has led astray, there is no guide for him. Its evidence is ﴿Whomever God leads astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 186].

وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ يمنعونهم من عذاب الله وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ.

Translation: ﴿And they have no helpers﴾, who would protect them from the punishment of God. ﴿And they swore by God with their most emphatic oaths that God will not raise up one who dies.﴾

الربيع عن أبي العالية قال: كان لرجل من المسلمين على رجل من المشركين دين فأتاه يتقاضاه فكان فيما تكلّم به: والذي أرجوه بعد الموت أنه لكذا، فقال المشرك: وإنك لتزعم أنك تبعث بعد الموت فأقسم بالله (لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ) فأنزل الله هذه الآية.

Translation: Al-Rabi' reported from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: A man from among the Muslims had a debt owed to him by a man from among the polytheists. He came to him to demand it, and among what he said was: "By the one I hope for after death, that it is such-and-such." The polytheist said: "Do you really claim that you will be raised after death?" and swore by God: ﴿God will not raise up one who dies.﴾ Then God revealed this verse.

قتادة: ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال لابن عبّاس: إن ناسا بالعراق يزعمون أن عليا مبعوث قبل يوم القيامة ويتأولون هذه الآية.

Translation: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Some people in Iraq claim that 'Ali will be raised before the Day of Resurrection, and they interpret this verse [in support of that]."

فقال ابن عبّاس: كذب أولئك، إنما هذه الآية عامة للناس، لو كان عليّ مبعوثا قبل يوم القيامة ما نكحنا نساءه ولا قسمنا ميراثه، قال الله ردا عليهم: بَلى وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ.

Translation: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Those people are liars. This verse is general for all people. If 'Ali were raised before the Day of Resurrection, we would not have married his wives, nor divided his inheritance." God said, refuting them: ﴿Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth, but most people do not know.﴾

في الخبر أن الله تعالى يقول: كذّبني ابن آدم ولم يكن له أن يكذبني، وشتمني ابن آدم ولا ينبغي له أن يشتمني، وأمّا تكذيبه إياي فحلفه بي أن لا أبعث الخلق، وأمّا شتمه إياي فقوله اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً وأنا الله الواحد الصمد الذي لم ألد ولم أولد ولم يكن لي كُفُواً أَحَدٌ.

Translation: It is reported in a report that God, exalted is He, says: "The son of Adam has denied Me, and it was not his right to deny Me; and the son of Adam has reviled Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me. As for his denial of Me, it is his swearing by Me that I will not raise up creation; and as for his reviling of Me, it is his saying: ﴿God has taken a son﴾. But I am God, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not begotten and has not been begotten, and there is none comparable to Me."

لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ هو مردود إلى قوله: لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ بَلى وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا يبين لهؤلاء المنكرين المقتسمين الذين يختلفون وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كاذِبِينَ.

Translation: ﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾: this refers back to His saying: ﴿God will not raise up one who dies. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth.﴾ He makes clear to these deniers, the ones who divided [the oath] and differed [among themselves]. ﴿And that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.﴾

إِنَّما قَوْلُنا لِشَيْءٍ الآية، يقول الله جل ثناؤه وتقدست أسماؤه: إنا إذا أردنا أن نبعث من يموت فلا تعب علينا ولا نصب في إحيائهم ولا في غير ذلك [مما نخلق ونكون ونحدث] ، لأنا إذا أردنا خلق شيء وإنشاؤه أَنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ [[تفسير الطبري: 14/ 141.]] .

Translation: ﴿Our word to a thing, when We intend it, is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ God, majestic is His praise and sanctified are His names, says: When We intend to raise up one who has died, there is no toil upon Us nor fatigue in bringing them to life, nor in anything else [that We create, bring into being, or originate], because when We intend to create a thing and bring it into being, We only say to it, "Be," and it is. [See al-Tabari's tafsir 14/141.]

وفي هذه الآية دليل على أنّ القرآن غير مخلوق، فذكر أن الله عزّ وجلّ أخبر أنه إذا أراد شيئا قال لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ، فلو كان قوله كُنْ مخلوقا لاحتاج إلى قول ثان ولاحتاج ذلك القول إلى قول ثالث إلى ما لا نهاية فلما بطل ذلك ثبت أن الله خلق الخلق بكلام غير مخلوق.

Translation: In this verse there is evidence that the Qur'an is uncreated. He mentioned that God, mighty and majestic, informed that when He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is. If His saying "Be" were created, it would require a second saying, and that saying would require a third, and so on without end. Since this is impossible, it is established that God created creation through uncreated speech.

He did not say "in the mouths" (bi-afwah).

the skin of the buffaloes has bitten their necks."
He did not say "skins" (juluwd).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 16, verse 51–60:

﴿And Allah said: Do not take two gods. He is only one God, so fear Me alone.﴾ ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is obedience and sincere devotion (al-din al-ta'a wa'l-ikhlas).﴾

Wasiban: constant, enduring, steadfast.

Ibn 'Abbas said: wajiban (obligatory). The meaning of the verse is that there is no one to whom obedience is owed and who is obeyed except that it ceases through decline or death, other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; obedience to Him endures and remains (wasiban) without interruption.

Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

"I do not seek a little praise whose lasting is short, / a day of blaming Time, all of it, enduring (wasiban)." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/5; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/114.]]

That is, constantly.

al-Farra' said: It is also said: sincere (khalisan).

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description (mathal al-su')﴾, that is, for those who attribute daughters to Allah: their need for offspring, their hatred of females among them, or their killing them out of fear of poverty, and their acknowledgment against themselves of shame.

Because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "The greatest of the major sins is that you invoke a rival to Allah while He created you, that you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you, and that you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." [5] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/62; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/75.]]

﴿And to Allah belongs the sublime description (al-mathal al-a'la)﴾: the lofty attribute, which is tawhid and sincere devotion.

Ibn 'Abbas said: mathal al-su' is the Fire, and al-mathal al-a'la is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/119.]]

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 16, verses 61–64:

﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it (the earth's surface) a single creature.﴾ "Upon it" (ʿalayhā), meaning on the surface of the earth, is a metonymy for something not mentioned. ﴿But He gives them respite until a specified term.﴾ That is, He grants them time upon it until the end of their lifespans. ﴿So when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ And it is not said that there is a death before it. ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike for themselves,﴾ meaning daughters. ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best (al-ḥusnā).﴾ The position of (anna), in the accusative, is a substitution (badal) for "the lie," because it is an explanation and rendering of it.

Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan recited (al-Kudhub) with a ḍammah on the kāf, the dhāl and the bāʾ, as an adjective (naʿt) of "al-alsina" (tongues). And "al-kudhub" is the plural of "kadhūb," like "rasūl" and "rusul," "ṣabūr" and "ṣabr," "shakūr" and "shukr."

﴿That for them is the best,﴾ meaning certainty. The sense of the verse: they assign daughters to Allah and claim that they themselves have sons.

Ḥayyān said: by "al-ḥusnā" is meant Paradise in the afterlife, if Muhammad was truthful about resurrection.

﴿Certainly (lā jarama)﴾ means truly. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it means "Yes" (balā).¹

﴿That for them is the Fire in the Hereafter, and that they are ﴾ mufraṭūn, meaning forgotten (mansiyyūn) in the Fire.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: mubʿadūn (kept far away).

Muqātil: matrūkūn (left behind).

Qatādah: muʿajjalūn ilā al-nār (hastened toward the Fire).

al-Farrāʾ: muqaddamūn ʿalā al-nār (brought forward before the Fire).

Nāfiʿ recited (mufrinūn) with a kasrah on the rāʾ and light emphasis, meaning musrifūn (wasteful). Abū Jaʿfar recited with a kasrah on the rāʾ and shaddah, meaning muḍayyiʿūn (those who neglect the command of Allah, exalted is He).

﴿By Allah, We certainly sent (messengers) to nations before you,﴾ just as We sent you to this community, ﴿but Satan made their deeds appear fair to them,﴾ the evil deeds in which they persisted. ﴿So he is their guardian today,﴾ their helper, their companion, and the one who manages their affairs, ﴿and for them is a painful punishment,﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿And We did not send down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that over which they differ,﴾ of religion and rulings, ﴿and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾ The words "guidance and mercy" are coordinated (ʿaṭf) with the position of His saying "li-tubayyina" (that you may make clear), because its place is in the accusative. The meaning of the speech is: "And We did not send down to you the Book except as an explanation for mankind, and as guidance and mercy."
