﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by forbidding that to them, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾, so We recompensed them for their rebellion. ﴿Then indeed your Lord, toward those who do evil in ignorance...﴾ and so on. It has been said that the pronoun in the phrase that follows refers to "ignorance" (jahala). It has also been said that it refers to "disobedience" (ma'siyah), because evil (su') means disobedience, so the pronoun was returned to the meaning. It has also been said that it refers to "the deed" (fi'lah).

﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah﴾, meaning a teacher of good who is followed by the people of the world, and he combined in himself the praiseworthy qualities and beautiful characteristics that would be found in a whole community (ummah).

al-Sha'bi narrated from Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said, ﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright﴾. I said: "Allah only said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah, devoutly obedient﴾." He said: "Do you know what an ummah is and what devoutly obedient (qanit) is?" I said: "Allah knows best." He said: "The ummah is one who teaches good, and the qanit is one who is obedient to Allah." And likewise Mu'adh ibn Jabal was: he taught good and was obedient to Allah and His Messenger.

Mujahid said: He was a believer alone while all the people were disbelievers. Qatadah said: There was no religious community except that they professed it and approved of him.

Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The earth has never been without fourteen (persons) through whom Allah averts (harm) from the people of the earth and brings forth its blessings, except in the time of Abraham, for he was alone, ﴿devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, a Muslim, steadfast upon the religion of Islam﴾, and ﴿he was not among the polytheists﴾. ﴿Grateful for His favors, He chose him and guided him to a straight path.﴾ And ﴿We gave him good in this world﴾, meaning prophethood, wisdom, and a good reputation.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It means the prayers in the saying of this community: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham." [And it has been said:] righteous offspring in old age. It has also been said: general acceptance among all nations. ﴿And indeed, in the Hereafter, he is among the righteous.﴾ Then ﴿We revealed to you: follow the religion of Abraham, upright, and he was not among the polytheists.﴾

Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to Abraham (peace be upon him) and took him to Mina, and prayed with him all the prayers: Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha', and Fajr. Then he went with him in the morning to Arafat, and prayed with him the two prayers together, Dhuhr and 'Asr. Then he set out and stood with him until the sun set, then he brought him back to Jam' (Muzdalifah), and prayed with him the two prayers, Maghrib and 'Isha'. Then he spent the night with him, and when it was the time when no one among the Muslims prays early, he prayed Fajr with him. Then he stood until it was the time when no one among the Muslims prays late, then he brought him back to Mina, threw the pebbles at the jamrah, sacrificed, and shaved, then he brought him to the House and circumambulated it with him." [[10]] So Allah revealed to Muhammad: ﴿Follow the religion of Abraham, upright, and he was not among the polytheists﴾ [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/134.]].

﴿The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed concerning it﴾. It means: Allah did not prescribe the glorifying and prohibition of the Sabbath except upon those who differed concerning it.

Some of them said: It is the greatest of days, because Allah finished creating things on Friday, then "rested" (sabata) on Saturday.

Others said: Rather, Allah made Sunday the greatest, because it is the day on which Allah began the creation of things, and they chose to glorify other than what Allah had commanded them to glorify, and they abandoned glorifying Friday, which Allah had commanded them to glorify, and they considered it lawful (to disregard it).

al-Kalbi said: Musa commanded them concerning Friday, saying: "Devote yourselves to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, one day in every seven days, worship Him on Friday, and do not work on it at your trades, and six days are for your trades." But they refused to accept this and said: "We want only the day which Allah has appointed from creation, which is Saturday." So it was made obligatory upon them and strictness was imposed upon them concerning it.

Then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam came to them with Friday, and they said: "We do not want their festival to be after our festival," meaning the Jews, and they adopted [the day of] Sunday. So Allah said: ﴿The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed concerning it.﴾

Qatadah said: ﴿Those who differed concerning it﴾ means the Jews; some of them considered it lawful and some of them forbade it.

Hammam ibn Munabbih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the last (in time) but the first (in precedence) on the Day of Resurrection, though they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. This is their day which was enjoined upon them, but they differed concerning it, so Allah guided us to it. So people follow us in this: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow." [[11]] [[Kitab al-Umm of al-Shafi'i: 1/217, and Musnad Ahmad: 2/312.]]

The Jew said: "Allah did not choose Abu al-Qasim above mankind." Umar, peace be upon him, raised his hand and slapped his eye. The Jew said: "Between me and you is Abu al-Qasim." ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord﴾, that is, the religion of your Lord, ﴿with wisdom﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿and good admonition﴾, meaning the admonitions of the Qur'an, ﴿and argue with them in the way that is best﴾, meaning: dispute and debate with them in the manner that is best.

The exegetes said: Turn away from their harm and do not fall short in conveying the message and calling to the truth, and it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of fighting. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided. And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished.﴾

Most of the exegetes said: Surah al-Nahl is entirely Meccan except for three verses, from ﴿And if you punish﴾ to its end, for they were revealed in Medina concerning the martyrs of Uhud. That was because the Muslims, when they saw what the polytheists had done to their dead at Uhud, slitting open the bellies, cutting off the private parts, and the evil mutilation, so that no one among the Muslim dead was left unmutilated except Hanzalah the monk—his father Abu ʿĀmir the monk had been with Abu Sufyan, so they left Hanzalah because of that—the Muslims said when they saw that: "If Allah gives us victory over them, we will surely exceed their conduct, and we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no Arab has ever inflicted upon anyone, and we will do and do..." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood over his uncle Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose nose and ears had been cut off, whose private parts had been cut off, and whose belly had been split open. Hind bint Utbah had taken a piece of his liver, chewed it, then spat it out, but it did not remain in her stomach until she vomited it up. The news reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said:

"As for her, if she had eaten it, she would never enter the Fire. Hamzah is too honored by Allah to let any part of his body enter the Fire." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at his uncle Hamzah, he looked at something that had never pained his heart more than that, and he (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy upon you, for I knew you were always doing good deeds and maintaining the ties of kinship. Had it not been for the grief of those after you over you, I would have been pleased to leave you until you are gathered from the mouths of beasts. By Allah, if Allah grants me victory over them, I will mutilate seventy of them in your place." [[13]] [[al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 3/197, and Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 192.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak said: This was before the revelation of Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah), when the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to fight only those who fought him and not to initiate fighting. But when Allah strengthened Islam and its people, and Bara'ah was revealed, and they were commanded to engage in jihad, this verse was abrogated.

Others said: Rather, this verse is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated), and it was only revealed concerning one who has been wronged: it is not lawful for him to inflict upon the wrongdoer more than the wrongdoer inflicted upon him. He is commanded to retaliate or to pardon, and he is forbidden to transgress. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri, Mujahid, and Ibn Sirin. Then He said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not except by Allah﴾, meaning by Allah's help and His success, ﴿and do not grieve over them﴾ in their turning away from you, ﴿and do not be in distress﴾.

Ibn Kathir read it with a kasrah on the dad here and in Surah al-Nahl; the rest read it with a fathah. Abu 'Ubayd chose this and said: "Because dayq (distress) refers to scarcity of livelihood and dwellings, but what is in the heart and chest is dayq (with fathah)."

Abu ʿAmr and the people of Basra said: ḍayq with a fathah on the dad means grief, and ḍiyq with a kasrah means hardship (al-shiddah).

al-Farra' and the people of Kufa said: They are two well-known dialects in the speech of the Arabs, like ratl and ratl.

Ibn Qutaybah said: ḍayq is a lightened form of ḍayyiq, like hayn and hayyin, layn and layyin, and according to this interpretation its description is as if He said: "And do not be in a distressing matter."

﴿From what they plot﴾, meaning from their scheming. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾, with help and victory.

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus, from Abu Qaza'ah, from Haram ibn Hayyan, and they said to him: "Advise us."

﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah﴾, meaning a teacher of good who is followed by the people of the world, and he combined in himself the praiseworthy qualities and beautiful characteristics that would be found in a whole community (ummah).

al-Sha'bi narrated from Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said, ﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright﴾. So they came to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Jew said: "Umar claims that Allah has chosen you above mankind, and I claimed that Allah has not chosen you above mankind, so he raised his hand and slapped me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for you, O Umar, satisfy him for your slap. Yes, O Jew: Adam is the chosen of Allah, Abraham is the friend of Allah, Musa is the one who spoke with Allah, ʿĪsā is the spirit of Allah, and I am the beloved of Allah. Yes, O Jew, there are two of the names of Allah the Exalted with which He named my community: He named Himself al-Salam (the Peace) and named my community al-Muslimun, and He named Himself al-Mu'min (the Giver of Security) and named my community al-Mu'minun. Yes, O Jew, you were given a day and it was stored up for us—meaning Friday—so today is our festival, tomorrow is yours, and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians. Yes, O Jew, you are the first and we are the last but first on the Day of Resurrection. Yes, O Jew, Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until I enter it, and it is forbidden to the nations until my community enters it." [[12]] [[al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah: 7/444, no. 162.]]

﴿Invite to the way of your Lord﴾, that is, the religion of your Lord, ﴿with wisdom﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿and good admonition﴾, meaning the admonitions of the Qur'an, ﴿and argue with them in the way that is best﴾, meaning: dispute and debate with them in the manner that is best.

The exegetes said: Turn away from their harm and do not fall short in conveying the message and calling to the truth, and it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of fighting. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided. And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished.﴾

Most of the exegetes said: Surah al-Nahl is entirely Meccan except for three verses, from ﴿And if you punish﴾ to its end, for they were revealed in Medina concerning the martyrs of Uhud. That was because the Muslims, when they saw what the polytheists had done to their dead at Uhud, slitting open the bellies, cutting off the private parts, and the evil mutilation, so that no one among the Muslim dead was left unmutilated except Hanzalah the monk—his father Abu ʿĀmir the monk had been with Abu Sufyan, so they left Hanzalah because of that—the Muslims said when they saw that: "If Allah gives us victory over them, we will surely exceed their conduct, and we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no Arab has ever inflicted upon anyone, and we will do and do..." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood over his uncle Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose nose and ears had been cut off, whose private parts had been cut off, and whose belly had been split open. Hind bint Utbah had taken a piece of his liver, chewed it, then spat it out, but it did not remain in her stomach until she vomited it up. The news reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said:

"As for her, if she had eaten it, she would never enter the Fire. Hamzah is too honored by Allah to let any part of his body enter the Fire." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at his uncle Hamzah, he looked at something that had never pained his heart more than that, and he (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy upon you, for I knew you were always doing good deeds and maintaining the ties of kinship. Had it not been for the grief of those after you over you, I would have been pleased to leave you until you are gathered from the mouths of beasts. By Allah, if Allah grants me victory over them, I will mutilate seventy of them in your place." [[13]] [[al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 3/197, and Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 192.]]

So Allah revealed: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾, the verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rather, we will be patient," [[14]] and he refrained from what he intended and expiated his oath.

Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak said: This was before the revelation of Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah), when the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to fight only those who fought him and not to initiate fighting. But when Allah strengthened Islam and its people, and Bara'ah was revealed, and they were commanded to engage in jihad, this verse was abrogated.

Others said: Rather, this verse is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated), and it was only revealed concerning one who has been wronged: it is not lawful for him to inflict upon the wrongdoer more than the wrongdoer inflicted upon him. He is commanded to retaliate or to pardon, and he is forbidden to transgress. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri, Mujahid, and Ibn Sirin. Then He said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not except by Allah﴾, meaning by Allah's help and His success, ﴿and do not grieve over them﴾ in their turning away from you, ﴿and do not be in distress﴾.

Ibn Kathir read it with a kasrah on the dad here and in Surah al-Nahl; the rest read it with a fathah. Abu 'Ubayd chose this and said: "Because dayq (distress) refers to scarcity of livelihood and dwellings, but what is in the heart and chest is dayq (with fathah)."

Abu ʿAmr and the people of Basra said: ḍayq with a fathah on the dad means grief, and ḍiyq with a kasrah means hardship (al-shiddah).

al-Farra' and the people of Kufa said: They are two well-known dialects in the speech of the Arabs, like ratl and ratl.

Ibn Qutaybah said: ḍayq is a lightened form of ḍayyiq, like hayn and hayyin, layn and layyin, and according to this interpretation its description is as if He said: "And do not be in a distressing matter."

﴿From what they plot﴾, meaning from their scheming. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾, with help and victory.

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus, from Abu Qaza'ah, from Haram ibn Hayyan, and they said to him: "Advise us."

He said: "I advise you with the last verses of Surah al-Nahl: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom﴾ to the end of the surah."

وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا ما قَصَصْنا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ ﴿And We had forbidden to those who became Jews what We have already related to you﴾, meaning in Surah al-An'am, where He says: ﴿And to those who became Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 146.]] and so on.

﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by forbidding that to them, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾, so We recompensed them for their rebellion. ﴿Then indeed your Lord, toward those who do evil in ignorance...﴾ and so on. It has been said that the pronoun in the phrase that follows refers to "ignorance" (jahala). It has also been said that it refers to "disobedience" (ma'siyah), because evil (su') means disobedience, so the pronoun was returned to the meaning. It has also been said that it refers to "the deed" (fi'lah).

﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah﴾, meaning a teacher of good who is followed by the people of the world, and he combined in himself the praiseworthy qualities and beautiful characteristics that would be found in a whole community (ummah).

al-Sha'bi narrated from Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said, ﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright﴾. I said: "Allah only said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah, devoutly obedient﴾." He said: "Do you know what an ummah is and what devoutly obedient (qanit) is?" I said: "Allah knows best." He said: "The ummah is one who teaches good, and the qanit is one who is obedient to Allah." And likewise Mu'adh ibn Jabal was: he taught good and was obedient to Allah and His Messenger.

Mujahid said: He was a believer alone while all the people were disbelievers. Qatadah said: There was no religious community except that they professed it and approved of him.

Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The earth has never been without fourteen (persons) through whom Allah averts (harm) from the people of the earth and brings forth its blessings, except in the time of Abraham, for he was alone, ﴿devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, a Muslim, steadfast upon the religion of Islam﴾, and ﴿he was not among the polytheists﴾. ﴿Grateful for His favors, He chose him and guided him to a straight path.﴾ And ﴿We gave him good in this world﴾, meaning prophethood, wisdom, and a good reputation.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It means the prayers in the saying of this community: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham." [And it has been said:] righteous offspring in old age. It has also been said: general acceptance among all nations. ﴿And indeed, in the Hereafter, he is among the righteous.﴾ Then ﴿We revealed to you: follow the religion of Abraham, upright, and he was not among the polytheists.﴾

Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to Abraham (peace be upon him) and took him to Mina, and prayed with him all the prayers: Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha', and Fajr. Then he went with him in the morning to Arafat, and prayed with him the two prayers together, Dhuhr and 'Asr. Then he set out and stood with him until the sun set, then he brought him back to Jam' (Muzdalifah), and prayed with him the two prayers, Maghrib and 'Isha'. Then he spent the night with him, and when it was the time when no one among the Muslims prays early, he prayed Fajr with him. Then he stood until it was the time when no one among the Muslims prays late, then he brought him back to Mina, threw the pebbles at the jamrah, sacrificed, and shaved, then he brought him to the House and circumambulated it with him." [[10]] So Allah revealed to Muhammad: ﴿Follow the religion of Abraham, upright, and he was not among the polytheists﴾ [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/134.]].

﴿The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed concerning it﴾. It means: Allah did not prescribe the glorifying and prohibition of the Sabbath except upon those who differed concerning it.

Some of them said: It is the greatest of days, because Allah finished creating things on Friday, then "rested" (sabata) on Saturday.

Others said: Rather, Allah made Sunday the greatest, because it is the day on which Allah began the creation of things, and they chose to glorify other than what Allah had commanded them to glorify, and they abandoned glorifying Friday, which Allah had commanded them to glorify, and they considered it lawful (to disregard it).

al-Kalbi said: Musa commanded them concerning Friday, saying: "Devote yourselves to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, one day in every seven days, worship Him on Friday, and do not work on it at your trades, and six days are for your trades." But they refused to accept this and said: "We want only the day which Allah has appointed from creation, which is Saturday." So it was made obligatory upon them and strictness was imposed upon them concerning it.

Then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam came to them with Friday, and they said: "We do not want their festival to be after our festival," meaning the Jews, and they adopted [the day of] Sunday. So Allah said: ﴿The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed concerning it.﴾

Qatadah said: ﴿Those who differed concerning it﴾ means the Jews; some of them considered it lawful and some of them forbade it.

Hammam ibn Munabbih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the last (in time) but the first (in precedence) on the Day of Resurrection, though they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. This is their day which was enjoined upon them, but they differed concerning it, so Allah guided us to it. So people follow us in this: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow." [[11]] [[Kitab al-Umm of al-Shafi'i: 1/217, and Musnad Ahmad: 2/312.]]
